output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: org.codehaus.plexus.util.cli.shell.Shell#getQuotingTriggerChars returns DEFAULT_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS = { ' ' }. CmdShell and CommandShell do not override it, so getRawCommandLine only quotes tokens containing a space. Metacharacter-only tokens (e.g. "ping&calc") reach cmd.exe/command.com via `getShellCommandLine` -> Commandline.getShellCommandline -> Runtime.exec unquoted; because cmd.exe strips the outer wrapping quotes when it finds special characters, the metacharacters get interpreted, allowing command injection through a tainted executable or argument.

Fix: Added `private static final char[] CMD_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS = { ' ', '&', '|', '<', '>', '(', ')', '^', '%' }` and an override of `getQuotingTriggerChars()` in both CmdShell and CommandShell, mirroring the mitigation BourneShell already applies for Unix. Tokens containing these characters are now quoted, so metacharacters remain inside quotes after cmd.exe's quote handling and are treated literally instead of as command separators/redirections.

Behavior preserved: Plain executables/arguments are unaffected (verified by testPlainExecutableIsNotOverQuoted, which still yields the single CmdShell wrapping `"chmod"`). Space-containing paths already received the same double-quote treatment, so the change is consistent with existing working behavior. Default shell on Linux is BourneShell, so no existing tests changed; CmdShellTest directly instantiates CmdShell to exercise the Windows path.
output_json.risk_notes: Quoting (rather than caret-escaping) is the mechanism used, consistent with the library's existing CmdShell double-quote wrapping and BourneShell approach; it prevents metacharacter interpretation for the common injection vectors. Embedded double-quote (") breakout is a distinct, pre-existing concern not addressed here (the base Shell does not enable double-quote escaping for these shells); '"' was intentionally left out of the trigger set to avoid producing malformed output given escaping is disabled. This fix cannot be dynamically verified on Windows in this Linux CI container, so validation is via string-level assertions on the generated command line. No POV was provided; reasoning is from the alert and code flow.
output_json.summary: Fixed a CWE-078 OS command injection gap in the Windows shell wrappers of plexus-utils. The base Shell quotes executable/argument tokens only when they contain a space (DEFAULT_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS = { ' ' }). BourneShell already overrides this with a metacharacter-aware set (BASH_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS), closing the injection hole on Unix, but CmdShell and CommandShell inherited the space-only set. As a result, an executable or argument containing cmd.exe/command.com metacharacters (& | < > ( ) ^ %) but no space was passed into `cmd.exe /X /C "..."` unquoted, letting an attacker terminate the intended command and inject additional commands. The fix gives both Windows shells a metacharacter-aware quoting-trigger set so such tokens are quoted exactly like space-containing paths already are (the existing, working double-quote wrapping), neutralizing the metacharacters. Added CmdShellTest to lock in the behavior; the full suite (286 tests) passes.
